quest.title: Every Aspect of a Warrior
quest.description: "What we trainers pursue, myself included, isn't success..."
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x35000

dialogues.speaker: Acomitl
dialogues.text: Why must I persist? Why can't I just give up...? Forget it, I give up! Help me, Manyoya.

dialogues.speaker: Matahga
dialogues.text: What an embarrassment! Stop acting like a child and giving up whenever things don't go smoothly. How can you even call yourself a warrior? I'm ashamed to call you my brother.

dialogues.speaker: Acomitl
dialogues.text: And are you telling me you've never been stumped and needed help?

dialogues.speaker: Matahga
dialogues.text: I have, which is why I'm here to get Father and Manyoya's opinions on the fruits of my special training. I'm not a coward like you!

dialogues.speaker: Manyoya
dialogues.text: Acomitl, I believe the captain rejected your resignation so that you could give it more thought. Don't make important decisions in the heat of things.

dialogues.speaker: Manyoya
dialogues.text: Calm down and make your own choice. The most important thing is that you don't come to regret it.

dialogues.speaker: Manyoya
dialogues.text: I'm retired, and even I don't know what the future holds for me, so I fear I haven't the right to give you any guidance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! So you three are siblings!

response.speaker: All Three Together
response.text: It's you two!?

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: My apologies, dear benefactor. My escape plan fell through.

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: Is there no way for me to escape this pain? Being a warrior is so exhausting. Why can't everything be simpler?
Still preoccupied with thoughts of the flying squad?
I'm sorry, Acomitl. Based on my experience, things don't get simpler that way.
Still, I just finished repairing Matahga's arm guards. Manyoya, do yours's need any work? Hmm? We have guests.

response.speaker: Manyoya
response.text: Ah, they're adventurers we met during our training away from home, father. They even helped Acomitl out.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Then greetings, kind friends. I'm Xueyoni, a training master and their father.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Acomitl seems to be in terrible condition, so let us know if you need help.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Thank you for the offer, but I think Acomitl is completely fine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You intend to just leave him be?

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Haha! What I'm trying to say is... Let's put it this way. You're adventurers, so you must have joined the Adventurers' Guild, right?

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Now that's an amazing organization. You adventurers desire to explore the world, right?

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Even so, I imagine every adventurer has their motivations. Some explore for the money, others desire knowledge, and some are just bored of doing nothing.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: So, it's a most impressive feat the Adventurers' Guild has achieved in uniting all those people under one banner.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Take me for example. I'm an old man who retired after serving as a Saurian rider in the flying squad and went on to become a master trainer in our tribe. Yet, I cannot imagine what a Guild containing the master trainers of all six tribes would look like.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... What does that have to do with Acomitl?

response.speaker: Manyoya
response.text: That's how our father explains things. Back when he was still in the flying squad, everyone there, even the Qucusaurs, would willingly hear his opinion.

response.speaker: Manyoya
response.text: He's now a master trainer for our tribe, and anyone who wishes to become a warrior comes to seek his advice, so relax — just listen for now.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Heh, that's all in the past, Manyoya. But I shall finish the tale all the same.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: We master trainers aspire toward the ideal of the "warrior." That's what inspires us to take the time and effort to design and set our training programs up.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: We all have a "dream warrior" we wish to see emerge, but no single person can dictate what such a warrior should be.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: We master trainers have found agreeing on any principles and regulations impossible, let alone forming a Guild.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: That "greatest warrior" has countless faces and personalities.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: They are strong-willed at times, but they sometimes struggle with self-doubt — not to mention how they will age and die.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Must warriors be immune to burnout? I can show you multiple woven scrolls that show how self-doubt and exhaustion plague everyone equally.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Must warriors be huge? I know of many who looked like giants yet were despicable beyond compare. Such are recorded upon woven scrolls too.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: And of course, warriors will decline, as the law of nature dictates.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: My kids call me a warrior, but look at me. I'm an old bird who doesn't fly anymore — I've no strength for it.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: A warrior with a perfect face, a person who conforms to every boring standard, will not be recognized as a hero here in Natlan.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Manyoya, Acomitl, Matahga, I've brought you here, for you are to be the heroes of the Flower-Feather Clan, gazing down from a great height.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Your worries and desires are fleeting states on a hero's long journey, not problems that need solving.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Does leaving the flying squad mean one is no longer a warrior? Does joining the flying squad automatically make one a warrior? There are no such things.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: It's okay to have ambitions, to hesitate, and to feel lost. You are a warrior, and a warrior must undergo trials to become a hero.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Accept how you are now, learn to live with that state, and overcome it. Never let it control you.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: This is the way of Natlan — the way of heroes. Do you understand?

response.speaker: Manyoya
response.text: I understand, Father.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Acomitl, are you still hesitating?

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Constant lectures aren't our family's way. Go fly with your brother and sister, just like when you were little.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Let your mind and body help you decide. Staying cooped up in the house and overthinking things won't lead to any good.

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: I got it, Father.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Do Master Trainers always speak so abstractly? Paimon didn't really get any of it. Did you, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Yep. Basically, this will involve a Gliding Challenge.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Adventurer, I've heard about you from my kids. You're a fascinating young person.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Having the guts to compete with Manyoya, help little Acomitl... and you even gained Matahga's recognition — a true warrior, you are.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: I'd like to invite you to fly with these kids. How about it?

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Haha, alright. When you've decided, come over and let us know.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: All three of my kids are top-tier fliers in the Flower-Feather Clan. You'll have a great time flying together.

choices.text: Nope. Family upbringing techniques are too profound.

dialogues.speaker: Matahga
dialogues.text: Another race? Haha! Just wait and see!

dialogues.speaker: Manyoya
dialogues.text: You're pretty confident. C'mon, Acomitl. We can't lose here!

dialogues.speaker: Acomitl
dialogues.text: Losing to you is whatever, but there's no way I'm losing to Matahga!

dialogues.speaker: Acomitl
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, be sure to give it your all, too. Don't fall for Matahga's late-game pushes. He's been doing that for ages.

dialogues.speaker: Acomitl
dialogues.text: When you're ready, let my father know, and we'll fly together.

talks.objective: Talk to Xueyoni to start the air race

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: Not bad, young one! Hahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: But you'll need more practice if you want to surpass my kids. Don't take it too hard, though! It's rare for anyone to achieve success in one go.

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: If you want to try again, just come find me.

dialogues.speaker: Matahga
dialogues.text: Haha! Sorry, but I pulled ahead this time!

dialogues.speaker: Acomitl
dialogues.text: Gah, Matahga, you annoying little... You've been like this since forever, always going all out in the second half!

dialogues.speaker: Matahga
dialogues.text: Feeling bitter? Catch me if you can, then! Haha!

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: You flew well, young one!

dialogues.speaker: Acomitl
dialogues.text: How was my flying just now?

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: Thanks for your encouragement, but I can tell you're still a cut above.

response.speaker: Matahga
response.text: Acomitl...

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: It's not what you think. I'm not discouraged because I can't outdo others. I can fly, I know I can.

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: Still, being in bad form for so long has ruined my self-confidence. I just can't approach flying with any sense of calm.

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: #{NICKNAME}'s different. {M#His}{F#Her} posture is way more relaxed. Anyone with eyes can see that.

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: Father, I know that you and sis want me to make up my own mind and not avoid the issue.

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: But if I told you now, that whether it's my body, my brain, or my heart...

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: That they all refuse to continue on a path that's not meant for me... Would you still support me?

response.speaker: Manyoya
response.text: It's okay, so long as it's your own decision, and you're willing to shoulder the consequences.

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: Matahga, will you...

response.speaker: Matahga
response.text: Hey! I'm not going to criticize you at a time like this. I've always known the sort of person you are, Big Brother.

response.speaker: Matahga
response.text: If you can't handle this, then just make a decisive break with it. As long as you stay true to yourself, you remain a warrior. No one has the right to criticize you.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Sometimes, the job of a Master Trainer is quite easy. I make training plans for warriors, but I don't have to take part myself.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: However, I, too, once flew around with Saurians day in and day out, and I know the true face of that kind of life.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Criticizing others is easy. Taking action is always harder.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: As a trainer, I suggest you request time off to recuperate both physically and mentally, even if it leads to dissatisfaction within the team.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: As your father, I know you don't want to continue, and I respect that choice.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: No longer being part of the flying squad isn't the end of the world. The warriors of the Flower-Feather Clan don't have to prove their worth through flying alone.

response.speaker: Acomitl
response.text: Thank you... I was worried you'd...

response.speaker: Manyoya
response.text: Don't overthink it. We're your family, and we'll always help you find a way, no matter what.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Being a warrior sure is tough! Paimon never imagined it would be this hard to join the Flower-Feather Clan's flying squad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that's right! Thinking about all the things we've encountered along the way, we've overcome them all. That's something we can be proud of, eh?

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: And if becoming a warrior isn't easy in itself, growing from a warrior into a hero is even more so.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: I've seen enough of the former to know when someone possesses the qualities needed to become the latter.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: You have undergone many trials, haven't you, youngster? I can see it in your eyes.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: It seems I wasn't mistaken. Your path differs from ours, and you might still have a ways to go. I'd be happy to assist a future hero.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: What's more, you've met and helped our family.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: If you want to use the training course here, just let me know. You can take off from here anytime.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Don't mention it. If anything, I'm eager to witness the moment you become a hero, resplendent in the skies.

choices.text: Not everyone can be a warrior.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's kinda strict, but it does make sense. Oh well, not like Paimon wanted to become one anyway, what with all that training every day.

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: Come and fly with my kids, young one. It's not every day you get to compete with the Flower-Feather Clan's finest.

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: Chase after the <color=#00E1FFFF>flying torch</color> on the course. Whoever catches it first wins. That's how I trained them when they were little.

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>The torch is held by a balloon decorated with red feathers</color>, symbolizing the responsibility and honor that a warrior should bear. I made it for them.

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: You'll recognize it once you see it. So, are you up for the contest?

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Haha, great! Let's head to the starting point and get ready then.

choices.text: I need a little more time.

response.speaker: Xueyoni
response.text: Let us know when you're ready then.

dialogues.speaker: Matahga
dialogues.text: #Aw, I lost again. Even after all that practice, I still lost to {M#him}{F#her}.

dialogues.speaker: Acomitl
dialogues.text: I told you this ages ago. There's no end to thinking about winning. Gotta admire your drive to just charge ahead without fear, though.

dialogues.speaker: Manyoya
dialogues.text: Well, you were like that when you were younger, too, following behind me every day, talking about how you wanted to become a master Saurian tamer...

dialogues.speaker: Acomitl
dialogues.text: Quit teasing me, sis...

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: You are all good children of mine, and fine warriors, too — and all warriors must face different challenges at different points...

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: Which is fine. So long as your consciences are clear, I am proud of you.

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: Not bad, young one! Hahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: But you'll need more practice if you want to surpass my kids. Don't take it too hard, though! It's rare for anyone to achieve success in one go.

dialogues.speaker: Xueyoni
dialogues.text: If you want to try again, just come find me.
